title: PhenoShared has inconsistent root identities
observation: README describes PhenoMLX/OMLX, root npm manifest names phenodocs, and Cargo workspace identifies substrate while listing absorbed shared domains.
interpretation: Entry-point and authority ambiguity can send agents to the wrong surface; consolidation is not yet proven by folder presence.
countercase: Some identities may be intentional independent components in a polyglot workspace; test package-level ownership rather than assuming corruption.
acceptance_proof: One accurate root map, distinct component manifests, exact source/release owners and clean consumer builds.

title: Tracera multi-project typecheck has a coverage hazard
observation: One tsc invocation repeats -p six times. A separate TypeScript 5.8.3 fixture reproduced last-project selection.
interpretation: The current command cannot be trusted as evidence that all six projects are checked.
countercase: Tracera locked compiler was not executed here; run the counterexample and actual project canaries on that exact release.
acceptance_proof: A seeded independent error in each eligible project fails the final gate, including the first and last; keep check side effects inside declared cache paths.

title: Typecheck contract test freezes command text rather than coverage
observation: Test asserts the exact multi--p command and disallows --build; path history ties it to PR 900 in August.
interpretation: An instrument can preserve a bad implementation while remaining green.
countercase: String assertions can be a secondary interface test, but cannot prove behavior.
acceptance_proof: Independent behavioral negative controls plus valid multi-project execution and revision binding.

title: A Tracera lint check invokes fixes
observation: lint:stylelint invokes lint:stylelint:fix before running stylelint.
interpretation: Read-only verification and repair are not cleanly separated.
countercase: An explicitly named repair pipeline may mutate; a gate must not silently rely on repairs.
acceptance_proof: Check-only run preserves tracked source and reports pre-existing defects; explicit fix command is separate.

title: Canonical JS migration is heterogeneous in live scripts
observation: Tracera uses Oxlint/Oxfmt; HeliosLab uses Biome; OmniRoute uses ESLint.
interpretation: Canonical choice is not consistently propagated through current entry points.
countercase: Fork contracts, plugins or framework rules may justify bounded retained tooling; docs-only grep would overstate this finding.
acceptance_proof: Rule-by-rule equivalence or strengthened coverage, formatter semantic parity, and actual clean consumer CI with a scoped residual-tool record when necessary.

title: PhenoDesign tool provenance is incompletely declared
observation: format calls oxfmt, but shown devDependencies omit it; tool dependencies use latest and packageManager is bare bun.
interpretation: Clean-room tool resolution, binary identity and update behavior require verification.
countercase: A lockfile or ancestor workspace can resolve versions; absence from this manifest alone does not prove build failure.
acceptance_proof: Declared tool source, frozen lock install, exact resolved binary version and formatter canary from outside a warm checkout.

title: Python metadata, lint target and execution need reconciliation
observation: AgilePlus requires Python >=3.14 but Ruff targets py312. Portage has uv/Ruff/ty and declares >=3.12.
interpretation: Compatibility minimum, lint syntax target and actual free-threaded runtime are different decisions.
countercase: Portage lower minimum can intentionally support upstream consumers; it does not prove the development interpreter is old.
acceptance_proof: Pin runtime per profile; import real dependency set; verify Py_GIL_DISABLED and GIL off; test races and align intended lint syntax.

title: FastMCP is present; shared implementation authority is not fully resolved
observation: Several current server paths import FastMCP and README paths refer to PhenoFastMCP. Similar lead_server paths exist in two trees.
interpretation: Start with source/release/consumer tracing, not creating another MCP framework.
countercase: Parallel paths may be packaging mirrors or intentional variants; full-file and lineage comparison remains unperformed.
acceptance_proof: One source writer per implementation, explicit mirrors, real package resolution, protocol/authorization/cancellation conformance in consumers.

title: A reusable workflow caller has an unresolved provider
observation: AgilePlus references phenotype-tooling sbom-monthly.yml@main. Provider lookup returns 404 in this connection.
interpretation: Both source location and mutable ref need attention.
countercase: 404 can mean access restriction or lifecycle changes, not necessarily deletion; hosted workflow success was not examined.
acceptance_proof: Resolve provider by immutable ID and permission, export actual workflow path at immutable ref, demonstrate hosted call and retained result.

title: Shared release optimization is size-oriented
observation: Shared Cargo release uses opt-level=z, LTO and one codegen unit while containing performance-oriented domains.
interpretation: There is no single universally optimal release profile for these products.
countercase: Size optimization may help instruction-cache behavior; this is not measured evidence of a slowdown.
acceptance_proof: Separate justified profile choices; compare whole-workload p95/p99, throughput, memory, size and build cost on intended hardware.

title: Authority documents have different dates and roles
observation: Registry references a May ecosystem count and a June language-tier policy; Shared has a September 16 pinned global handbook.
interpretation: Freshness and declared authority must be explicit; copy propagation must not create independent writers.
countercase: An older domain decision may still be compatible and valid; newest prose alone is not authority.
acceptance_proof: Field-level authority map and explicit supersession/compatibility links; no parallel registry.

title: Docs/design consumption exists in declarations but is not qualified
observation: Shared npm manifest declares @phenotype/docs workspace dependency and a Git design dependency; PhenoDesign exports themes/tokens/CSS.
interpretation: The problem is not simply that there is no shared docs/design layer; actual release and consumer contracts need proof.
countercase: Declared dependency may be unused, shadowed by local assets or intentionally development-only.
acceptance_proof: Isolated package install, imports/renderer reachability, generated API/version lineage, link and visual state tests on consumer artifacts.

title: Existing Lefthook is package-specific and uses ambient Python
observation: Infra Lefthook invokes Python wrappers around cargo commands for phenotype-infra and a local commit-message script.
interpretation: File presence does not establish interpreter reproducibility, current package coverage, installation, or cross-repo reuse.
countercase: Hooks may be intentionally scoped; ambient interpreter may be managed externally.
acceptance_proof: Resolve effective hook config, intended package set and toolchain; test nested-file selection, installation and equivalent mandatory CI gate.

title: Patch burden and dependency rewriting need semantic gates
observation: Tracera postinstall chains seven patch scripts; recent Shared history reports redaction followed by URL repairs.
interpretation: Mass transformations and local patches need typed scope, rationale, upstream linkage and clean-resolution proof.
countercase: Necessary upstream compatibility patches may be cheaper than a fork or rewrite; some redactions are required.
acceptance_proof: Patch registry with exit condition, exact dependency version coverage and canaries; no mutation of credentials or reintroduction of secrets.

title: Native TypeScript command name is not an adoption detector
observation: Shared declares TypeScript ^7.0.2; Tracera declares 5.9.3; upstream now calls native TypeScript tsc.
interpretation: A blanket replacement of every tsc occurrence with tsgo is incorrect.
countercase: Compiler-API consumers can need a separate JS implementation even when CLI checks are native.
acceptance_proof: Resolve CLI provider/version/hash separately from API dependencies; qualify framework emit/typecheck/editor paths.
